job_highlights.title: Responsibilities
items: Director, Advanced Data Scientist will provide senior strategic and technical leadership within the Partnership Division's data science and modeling function

This role is responsible for defining and executing multi-year modeling roadmap and overseeing the development and implementation of advanced machine learning models that support credit decisioning and portfolio management

The successful candidate will combine deep quantitative expertise with the organizational influence and executive presence required to shape strategy, drive cross-functional alignment, and deliver measurable business impact at scale
Vision and Strategy

Define and own the multi-year modeling roadmap for the development of several critical custom credit-risk acquisition and portfolio management models, establishing strategic priorities, sequencing, and investment rationale aligned with Partnership Division business objectives

Serve as a senior thought leader and decision-maker on modeling approaches, leading discussions with senior business, credit risk, first line of risk, compliance, and technology stakeholders to align methodology, priorities, and risk considerations

Identify and evaluate emerging modeling capabilities, analytical approaches, and implementation methods that can expand the division's competitive advantage in credit decisioning and customer risk management

Communicate modeling strategy, project status, and key results to senior leaders through clear, executive-ready reporting — translating complex quantitative findings into actionable business insights and ensuring leadership has the visibility needed to make informed decisions
Model Development
Independently design and develop advanced ML models for credit card acquisition and underwriting and account management and customer risk
Apply advanced statistical and machine learning techniques to large-scale customer and credit datasets
Evaluate and implement algorithms including gradient boosting, random forests, neural networks, generalized additive models, ensemble methods, survival models, and other advanced ML approaches
Conduct fair lending analysis (e.g., least discriminatory analysis)
Identify opportunities to improve model performance, stability, interpretability, and business value
End-to-End Model Ownership
Independently lead model-development projects from problem definition through production implementation
Translate business objectives into well-defined modeling frameworks, target variables, populations, and performance criteria
Perform feature engineering, variable selection, model development, hyperparameter optimization, and performance evaluation
Establish appropriate training, validation, and out-of-time testing strategies
Document modeling methodology, assumptions, limitations, and results
Partner with model validation and model risk management teams to address challenges and incorporate feedback
Advanced Analytics and Research
Conduct research on emerging ML techniques and assess their applicability to credit risk
Develop innovative approaches for extracting predictive signals from traditional and alternative data sources
Investigate nonlinear relationships, interactions, customer behavior patterns, and temporal dynamics that may not be captured by traditional credit-risk models
Develop interpretable ML approaches that balance predictive performance with regulatory and business requirements
Explore techniques such as explainable AI, causal modeling, ensemble learning, semi-supervised learning, and automated machine learning where appropriate
Model Performance and Monitoring
Develop model performance and stability monitoring frameworks
Monitor predictive performance, population shifts, variable stability, and model degradation
Identify emerging risks and recommend model recalibration, redevelopment, or replacement when appropriate
Conduct ongoing research to improve model performance and robustness
Technical Leadership
Serve as a subject-matter expert in advanced ML and credit-risk modeling
Establish best practices for ML model development, testing, documentation, and deployment
Stay current with advances in machine learning, credit-risk analytics, and regulatory expectations
Regardless of your location, you'll be fully integrated into our team through robust digital collaboration tools and regular communication

The Applied Data Scientist – AI Enablement is a high-impact individual contributor role focused on building internal AI capabilities and removing systemic constraints that limit HDR’s ability to scale artificial intelligence across the Transportation Business Group. In the initial phase, this role is primarily internally focused, developing AI solutions, improving data and technology foundations, and identifying bottlenecks in systems, processes, and tooling. What You Will Do

This position is open for external candidates only to apply.

The Earth and Environmental Sciences Division (EES), Energy and Natural Resources Security Group (EES-16) at Los Alamos National Laboratory is building next-generation artificial intelligence and data platforms that transform complex information into actionable intelligence for national security decision-makers. As a member of our team, you'll develop enterprise-scale data systems that power machine learning algorithms analyzing critical infrastructure helping the nation anticipate and respond to emerging threats.

Initially, you'll design, implement, and deploy scalable software systems supporting AI-enabled analytics and large-scale data integration. Responsibilities include developing production-quality Python code, designing APIs and data services, building cloud-native data pipelines, integrating heterogeneous data sources, and creating scalable analytics workflows for machine learning and scientific applications. You'll work with modern software engineering practices including version control, CI/CD, containerization, cloud-native architectures, and distributed computing, with opportunities to contribute to MLOps, DevSecOps, and advanced AI workflows that transition research into operational capabilities.

You'll collaborate with researchers and software engineers across multiple national laboratories and scientific disciplines-from computer science and mathematics to economics and engineering-to solve problems that transcend any single domain. Your work will span cloud-native architectures, large language models, knowledge graphs, and intelligent systems that augment human decision-making. This cross-disciplinary environment demands intellectual agility: you won't focus on a single technology stack but will rapidly acquire new skills and pivot between emerging technologies as national security priorities evolve.

This isn't abstract research. Your innovations will deploy in systems supporting government agencies protecting the nation's most vital assets. You'll thrive in a fast-paced environment where your ability to quickly learn and adapt is as valuable as your existing expertise. As AI advances and new threats emerge, you'll be at the forefront of innovation, constantly learning and applying cutting-edge technologies to mission-critical problems.

Unlike traditional positions focused on a single application, this role offers the opportunity to develop technologies supporting high-impact national security missions. Your success depends on openness to change, enthusiasm for learning in a fast-paced research environment, and ability to bridge disciplines and technologies as the national security landscape continuously transforms.

We anticipate hiring three (3) scientists for an initial two-year term appointment. During the early phase of the appointment, successful candidates will focus on data science and engineering, including building data pipelines and lakehouse capabilities using Databricks, developing AI models to identify and predict supply chain threats and vulnerabilities, and creating decision-support tools for the U.S. Department of Homeland Security.
